title: Calderon Zygmund Decomposition and Singular Integrals

items.title: Marcinkiewicz interpolation from weak (1,1) and strong (2,2)
items.statement: Let (X,μ) be a σ-finite measure space and let 1<p<2. Let T be a sublinear operator defined on L¹(X)+L²(X), of weak type (1,1) with constant A and strong type (2,2) with constant B. Then every f∈L^p(X) satisfies ‖Tf‖_p ≤ [p(2A/(p−1)+4B²/(2−p))]^{1/p}‖f‖_p.

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis
references.locator: Chapter 2, Theorem 2.4 and proof, printed pp. 27–29

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Theorem 1.3.2 and proof, printed pp. 33–36

items.strategy: Split f=f1+f2 at level t (f1=f on {|f|>t}, f2=f on {|f|≤t}); sublinearity gives {|Tf|>t}⊂{|Tf1|>t/2}∪{|Tf2|>t/2}; apply weak (1,1) to f1 and Chebyshev plus strong (2,2) to f2; integrate t^{p−1} over (0,∞), exchange by Tonelli, and evaluate the two inner integrals ∫_0^{|f|}(p−1)t^{p−2}dt and ∫_{|f|}^∞(2−p)t^{p−3}dt. Constants are explicit.

items.title: Calderón–Zygmund kernels and their associated operators
items.statement: Let n≥1. A Calderón–Zygmund kernel is a measurable k:ℝ^n\{0}→ℂ, integrable on compact subsets of ℝ^n\{0}, together with finite constants A₁,A₂ such that (i) sup_{R>0}∫_{R≤|x|≤2R}|k(x)|dx≤A₁, and (ii) sup_{y≠0}∫_{|x|≥2|y|}|k(x−y)−k(x)|dx≤A₂ (Hörmander's condition). A linear operator T:L²(ℝ^n)→L²(ℝ^n) with finite operator norm B is a Calderón–Zygmund operator with kernel k when Tf(x)=∫k(x−y)f(y)dy for a.e. x∉supp f, for every compactly supported f∈L²(ℝ^n). A principal-value distribution for k is a tempered distribution W that agrees with k on ℝ^n\{0} and for which some sequence δ_j↓0 satisfies ⟨W,φ⟩=lim_j∫_{|x|≥δ_j}k(x)φ(x)dx for every φ∈S(ℝ^n). Neither the existence of a principal-value distribution nor a truncation limit is assumed, and T need not be convolution with such a W; only the off-support representation is used.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: §5.3.2, conditions (5.3.4) and (5.3.12) and the setup (5.3.7)–(5.3.9), printed pp. 358–359

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4
references.locator: §2, Definitions 2.1 and 2.4, printed pp. 6–7

items.strategy: Fix the two kernel bounds on the annular and Hörmander scales and the off-support representation; record explicitly that the size condition is annular rather than pointwise and that no principal-value existence is part of the definition. The pointwise Hölder condition is a strictly stronger hypothesis recorded next, and its implication to (ii) is proved as a separate local lemma.

items.title: Standard (Hölder) Calderón–Zygmund kernels
items.statement: A Calderón–Zygmund kernel k is standard δ-Hölder, for some 0<δ≤1, with constant A₂'<∞ if |k(x−y)−k(x)|≤A₂'|y|^δ|x|^{−n−δ} whenever |x|≥2|y|>0. A Calderón–Zygmund operator is called a standard-kernel operator when its kernel is standard δ-Hölder. This pointwise condition is a sufficient hypothesis for the integral Hörmander condition of the base definition (proved as the next item); the converse is not claimed.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: §5.3.2, conditions (5.3.10)–(5.3.12) and the comparison sentence, printed p. 359

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4
references.locator: §2, Definition 2.1 and Remarks 2.3, printed pp. 6–7

items.strategy: Record the pointwise first-difference estimate on the regime |x|≥2|y|>0 with the Hölder exponent δ∈(0,1] kept explicit; state only the implication proved next and make no claim that the converse holds.

items.title: Standard Hölder kernels satisfy the Hörmander condition
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Every standard δ-Hölder Calderón–Zygmund kernel with constant A₂' is a Calderón–Zygmund kernel in the sense of the base definition, and its Hörmander constant may be taken to be A₂=|S^{n−1}|2^{−δ}δ^{−1}A₂'.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: §5.3.2, comparison of (5.3.11) with (5.3.12), printed p. 359

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis
references.locator: §3.8, footnote after (3.13): the smoothness condition implies the Hörmander condition, printed p. 11

items.strategy: Fix y≠0 and integrate the pointwise bound over {|x|≥2|y|}; polar coordinates and the substitution ρ=2|y|s give |S^{n−1}|∫_{2|y|}^∞ρ^{−1−δ}dρ =|S^{n−1}|(2|y|)^{−δ}/δ; multiply by A₂'|y|^δ.

items.title: Dyadic cubes of all generations in R^n
items.statement: Fix n≥1. For k∈ℤ and a function m:n→ℤ, the dyadic cube of generation k and index m is the half-open box Q_{k,m}={x∈ℝ^n: m_i2^{−k}<x_i≤(m_i+1)2^{−k} for every i<n}; its side length is 2^{−k} and its volume is 2^{−kn}. Generations are indexed by all of ℤ, so cubes of side 2^{|k|}>1 occur for k<0. The cubes with k≥0 are exactly those of [[def-dyadic-cube-in-rn|the measure-theory generation-k convention]], which is bounded above by the unit cube and does not suffice for stopping-time decompositions at small heights; the all-generations family below is the grid used by the dyadic maximal function and the Calderón–Zygmund decomposition on this page.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: §5.3.1, dyadic cube definition and nesting sentence preceding Theorem 5.3.1, printed p. 355

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis
references.locator: ch. 1 §1.2, definition of D_k for k∈ℤ and the transfer of properties (2)–(5) of Remark 1.1, printed pp. 9–10

items.strategy: Fix the half-open convention (m_i2^{−k},(m_i+1)2^{−k}] matching the published dyadic-cube item, regard the generation index as an integer, and record explicitly that the published grid has k≥0 only. Pointwise reformulation: m_i<2^kx_i≤m_i+1. The following item proves the partition, volume and nesting facts for this larger family.

items.title: All-generation dyadic cubes: partition, volume and nesting
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$ and use the all-generations dyadic cubes of
[[def-dyadic-cube-in-rn-all-generations]]. Then:

1. For every $k\in\mathbb Z$ the generation-$k$ dyadic cubes are pairwise
   disjoint and cover $\mathbb R^n$, and each has volume
   $|Q_{k,m}|=2^{-kn}$.
2. Every dyadic cube $Q$ of generation $k$ has, for each $j<k$, exactly one
   ancestor dyadic cube of generation $j$ containing $Q$; in particular the
   parent of $Q$ has generation $k-1$ and volume $2^n|Q|$.
3. If dyadic cubes $Q,Q'$ of generations $k\le k'$ intersect, then
   $Q'\subseteq Q$; consequently two dyadic cubes are either disjoint or one
   contains the other, and cubes of one generation are equal or disjoint.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: §5.3.1, printed p. 355: dyadic cubes of all integer generations are disjoint or nested

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis
references.locator: ch. 1 §1.2, printed pp. 9–10: C_k covers ℝ^n, pairwise disjointness, and properties (2)–(5) of Remark 1.1

items.strategy: Repeat the published generation-k argument with k,k'∈ℤ: reduce m_i<2^kx_i≤m_i+1 by the integer-part property (2^k>0 for every k∈ℤ), compute the volume as the product of the n equal side lengths 2^{−k}, and for (2)–(3) put d=k'−k≥0, M_i=m_i2^d and compare the coordinate intervals (a nested chain of integer intervals), using the integer order and power laws. All radii and indices are canonical, so no choice is used.

items.title: Maximal dyadic cubes above a level
items.statement:
Let $f\in L^1(\mathbb R^n)$ and $\lambda>0$, and let the dyadic cubes be the
all-generations cubes of [[def-dyadic-cube-in-rn-all-generations]]. The dyadic
cubes $Q$ with average $|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|f|>\lambda$ that are maximal under
inclusion form a countable family of pairwise disjoint cubes; their union is
exactly the dyadic maximal superlevel set $\{M_df>\lambda\}$, where
$$M_df(x)=\sup\Bigl\{|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|f|:Q\text{ dyadic},\ x\in Q\Bigr\}$$
over all generations; each such $Q$ satisfies
$|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|f|\le2^n\lambda$; and
$\sum_Q|Q|\le\lambda^{-1}\|f\|_1$.

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 3
references.locator: §4, Proposition 4.3 and its proof, printed pp. 23–24

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis
references.locator: Chapter 1, Theorem 1.12, printed pp. 12–14

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Theorem 5.3.1 and its proof, printed pp. 356–357

items.strategy: Call a cube bad if its average of |f| exceeds λ. Every bad cube satisfies |Q|<λ^{−1}‖f‖₁, so bad cubes have bounded side length; since ancestors are unique at each generation, the chain of bad ancestors of any bad cube is finite and has a coarsest member, which is maximal. Distinct maximal bad cubes are disjoint by the nesting property. If x lies in a maximal bad cube then M_d f(x)>λ; conversely a cube realizing an average above λ lies in a maximal bad cube containing x, so the union is exactly {M_d f>λ}. Each maximal bad cube has a good parent, whence the 2^nλ average bound; disjointness and the strict inequality against λ|Q| give Σ|Q|≤λ^{−1}‖f‖₁. The selection and the enumeration of the countable family are canonical, and no choice is used.

items.title: Radially decreasing kernels are dominated by the maximal function
items.statement:
Let $\omega\ge0$ be a measurable, radially nonincreasing, integrable function on
$\mathbb R^n$: that is, $\omega(x)=\omega(y)$ whenever $|x|=|y|$ and
$\omega(x)\ge\omega(y)$ whenever $|x|\le|y|$. Let
$f\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n)$. Then for every $x\in\mathbb R^n$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^n}|f(x-y)|\,\omega(y)\,dy\le\|\omega\|_1\,Mf(x),$$
where $M$ is the centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator and both sides may be
$+\infty$.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis
references.locator: Theorem 2.9 and its proof (decreasing-kernel domination), printed p. 5

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.3.4, the step bounding the error term by M(f), printed pp. 364–365

items.strategy: Layer-cake ω(y)=∫_0^{ω(0)}1_{ω>s}(y)ds, and note that each superlevel set is a ball B(0,r_s) up to a Lebesgue-null subset of its boundary (radial monotonicity makes the superlevel sets unions of full spheres). Tonelli and ∫_{B(x,r_s)}|f|≤|B(x,r_s)|Mf(x) give the bound; the same layer-cake identity computes ‖ω‖₁=∫_0^∞|B(0,r_s)|ds. The radii are canonical suprema, so no choice is used.

items.title: Calderón–Zygmund decomposition at height λ
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let f∈L¹(ℝ^n) and λ>0. Then f=g+Σ_j b_j a.e., where the cubes Q_j are the maximal all-generation dyadic cubes of the previous item, b_j=(f−|Q_j|^{−1}∫_{Q_j}f)1_{Q_j} satisfies ∫b_j=0 and ‖b_j‖₁≤2^{n+1}λ|Q_j|, and g=f outside ⋃_jQ_j and g=|Q_j|^{−1}∫_{Q_j}f on Q_j satisfies ‖g‖₁≤‖f‖₁, |g|≤2^nλ a.e. and ‖g‖₂²≤2^nλ‖f‖₁; moreover Σ_j|Q_j|≤λ^{−1}‖f‖₁.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Theorem 5.3.1, printed pp. 355–357

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 3
references.locator: §4, Proposition 4.3 and its proof, printed pp. 23–24

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis
references.locator: Chapter 1, Theorem 1.16, printed pp. 14–16

items.strategy: Use the maximal cubes of the previous item and set g,b_j as stated. On a bad cube the average bound of the previous item gives |g|≤2^nλ; off ⋃Q_j every dyadic cube through x is good, and the dyadic cubes through x shrink nicely to x, so the differentiation theorem gives |f(x)|≤λ a.e. there. The L¹ bound on b_j follows from the average bounds, and ‖g‖₂²≤‖g‖_∞‖g‖₁≤2^nλ‖f‖₁ from the pointwise and integral bounds on g.

items.title: The good part has controlled L² image
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let T be a Calderón–Zygmund operator with kernel constants A₁,A₂ and L² norm B, and let f=g+Σ_j b_j be the Calderón–Zygmund decomposition of f∈L¹(ℝ^n) at height λ>0. Then |{|Tg|>λ/2}|≤4B²2^nλ^{−1}‖f‖₁.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.3.3, treatment of the good part, printed pp. 360–362

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4
references.locator: Corollary 2.9, first term, printed p. 8

items.strategy: Chebyshev's inequality for |Tg|² gives |{|Tg|>λ/2}|≤(2/λ)²‖Tg‖₂²≤(2B/λ)²‖g‖₂², and ‖g‖₂²≤‖g‖_∞‖g‖₁≤2^nλ‖f‖₁ by the decomposition bounds.

items.title: The bad part is integrable away from expanded cubes
items.statement:
Let $T$ be a Calderón–Zygmund operator with kernel constants $A_1,A_2$
([[def-calderon-zygmund-kernel-and-principal-value-operator]]), let $Q$ be a
dyadic cube ([[def-dyadic-cube-in-rn-all-generations]]) with centre $c_Q$, and let
$b_Q\in L^2(\mathbb R^n)$ be supported in $Q$ with $\int b_Q=0$. If $Q^*$ is the
cube concentric with $Q$ whose side length is $2\sqrt n$ times the side length of
$Q$, then
$$\int_{\mathbb R^n\setminus Q^*}|Tb_Q(x)|\,dx\le A_2\|b_Q\|_1.$$

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.3.3: the cubes Q_j* of side 2√nℓ(Q_j) and the A₂ bound, printed pp. 362–363

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4
references.locator: Lemma 2.7 and its proof, printed pp. 7–8

items.strategy: For x∉Q* the off-support representation applies and ∫b_Q=0 gives Tb_Q(x)=∫_Q(k(x−y)−k(x−c_Q))b_Q(y)dy, using that b_Q is compactly supported and in L². The geometry x∉Q*, y∈Q gives |x−c_Q|≥2|y−c_Q| — this is why the dilation factor 2√n (not 3) is the smallest that works in every dimension — so the Hörmander bound integrates to A₂∫_Q|b_Q| after the Tonelli exchange. The Hörmander integral is applied with the origin shifted to c_Q, which the translation-invariant form of the condition permits.

items.title: Calderón–Zygmund operators are of weak type (1,1)
items.statement:
Let $T$ be a Calderón–Zygmund operator with kernel constants $A_1,A_2$ and $L^2$
norm $B$. Then for every $f\in L^1(\mathbb R^n)$ and every $\lambda>0$,
$$|\{|Tf|>\lambda\}|\le C_n(A_2+B)\lambda^{-1}\|f\|_1$$
with a dimensional constant $C_n$ independent of $T$, $f$ and $\lambda$;
equivalently, $T$ extends to a bounded operator
$L^1(\mathbb R^n)\to L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R^n)$.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Theorem 5.3.3, weak (1,1) part (5.3.13), and its proof, printed pp. 359–363

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4
references.locator: Corollary 2.9 and its proof, printed pp. 8–9

items.strategy: Apply the decomposition at height γλ and split |{|Tf|>λ}| by Tf=Tg+ΣTb_j; bound the good part with the L² estimate and Chebyshev; cover the enlarged cubes ⋃Q_j*; on the complement use the expanded-cube integrability and Chebyshev together with ‖b_j‖₁≤2^{n+1}γλ|Q_j|; choose γ small (a fixed multiple of A₂^{−1}) and sum Σ|Q_j|≤(γλ)^{−1}‖f‖₁.

items.title: The Lp range: interpolation below two and adjoint duality above two
items.statement:
Let $T$ be a linear operator defined on $L^1(\mathbb R^n)+L^2(\mathbb R^n)$ that
is bounded on $L^2(\mathbb R^n)$ with norm $B$, let $T^*$ denote its adjoint with
respect to the $L^2$ pairing, and suppose that $T$ and $T^*$ both satisfy the
weak $(1,1)$ bound $|\{|Tf|>\lambda\}|\le A\lambda^{-1}\|f\|_1$ for every
$f\in L^1(\mathbb R^n)$ and $\lambda>0$ (and likewise for $T^*$). Then for every
$1<p<\infty$, $p\ne2$, $T$ is bounded on $L^p(\mathbb R^n)$: for $1<p<2$ the
operator norm is at most
$$C_p:=\Bigl[p\Bigl(\frac{2A}{p-1}+\frac{4B^2}{2-p}\Bigr)\Bigr]^{1/p},$$
and for $2<p<\infty$ it is at most $C_{p'}$, the same expression evaluated at the
conjugate exponent $p'=p/(p-1)\in(1,2)$.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Theorem 5.3.3, the duality and interpolation argument for (5.3.14), printed pp. 362–363

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4
references.locator: Paragraph and Corollary 2.10 on interpolation, adjointness and duality, printed pp. 9–10

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis
references.locator: Chapter 2, Theorem 2.4, printed pp. 27–29

items.strategy: For 1<p<2 apply the Marcinkiewicz interpolation lemma to T, using that f∈L^p∩L² splits at height t into f1∈L¹∩L² and f2∈L², that sublinearity gives the pointwise domination by |Tf1|+|Tf2|, and that the weak (1,1) hypothesis applies to f1 while the strong (2,2) hypothesis applies to f2. For 2<p<∞ apply the same lemma to T* at the conjugate exponent p'∈(1,2); the pairing identity ⟨Tf,g⟩=⟨f,T*g⟩ for f∈L^p∩L² and g∈L^{p'}∩L² together with the L^{p'} norm-recovery identity and the density of smooth compactly supported functions transfers the bound to T, and density of L^p∩L² in L^p gives the unique extension.

items.title: Calderón–Zygmund operators are bounded on Lp
items.statement:
Let $T$ be a Calderón–Zygmund operator with kernel constants $A_1,A_2$ and $L^2$
norm $B$. Then for every $1<p<\infty$, $T$ extends uniquely to a bounded operator
on $L^p(\mathbb R^n)$ with
$$\|Tf\|_p\le C_{n,p}(A_2+B)\max\bigl(p,(p-1)^{-1}\bigr)\|f\|_p,$$
where $C_{n,p}$ depends only on $n$ and $p$.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Theorem 5.3.3, (5.3.14), and its proof, printed pp. 359–363

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4
references.locator: Corollary 2.10, printed p. 9

items.strategy: The transposed kernel k*(x)=k(−x) satisfies the same size and Hörmander bounds with the same constants, and T* has L² norm B, so T* is again a Calderón–Zygmund operator. Apply the weak (1,1) theorem to T and to T*, then the interpolation-and-duality lemma to T and T*.

items.title: Maximal truncated singular integrals
items.statement: Let k:ℝ^n\{0}→ℂ be locally integrable off the origin with |k(x)|≤A₁|x|^{−n}. For 1≤p<∞, f∈L^p(ℝ^n) and 0<ε<N<∞ define the truncated and doubly truncated integrals T_εf(x)=∫_{|y|>ε}k(y)f(x−y)dy and T^{(ε,N)}f(x)=∫_{ε<|y|<N}k(y)f(x−y)dy, both absolutely convergent for every x, and the maximal truncated operators T^*f(x)=sup_{ε>0}|T_εf(x)| and T^{**}f(x)=sup_{0<ε<N<∞}|T^{(ε,N)}f(x)|, with values in [0,∞]. Under the pointwise size bound one has T^*f≤T^{**}f≤2T^*f pointwise, so the two are comparable. No upper truncation and no principal-value existence are asserted by the definition itself.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis
references.locator: §3.8, definitions preceding Theorem 3.8, printed p. 11

items.strategy: Define the truncations and their suprema from the kernel alone. Absolute convergence for f∈L^p follows from Hölder because k·1_{|·|>ε}∈L^{p'}; the doubly truncated form is used in the maximal weak (1,1) proof so that no principal-value limit is presupposed. The comparability T^*≤T^{**}≤2T^* uses T^{(ε,N)}=T_ε−T_N together with dominated convergence in N under the pointwise size bound.

items.title: Cotlar's inequality for maximal truncations
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $k:\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\to\mathbb C$ satisfy the pointwise size bound
$|k(x)|\le A_1|x|^{-n}$, the $\delta$-Hölder smoothness bound
$|k(x-y)-k(x)|\le A_2'|y|^\delta|x|^{-n-\delta}$ for
$|x|\ge2|y|>0$ with $0<\delta\le1$, and the cancellation bound
$\sup_{0<r<R}|\int_{r<|x|<R}k(x)\,dx|\le A_3$. Let $W$ be a principal-value
distribution extending $k$ ([[def-calderon-zygmund-kernel-and-principal-value-operator]])
and let $T$ be the convolution operator with $W$, bounded on
$L^2(\mathbb R^n)$. Then for every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$ and almost
every $x$,
$$T^*f(x)\le M(Tf)(x)+C_{n,\delta}(A_1+A_2'+A_3)Mf(x),$$
where $M$ is the centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator of
[[def-centered-and-uncentered-hardy-littlewood-maximal-functions]] and $T^*$ is
the maximal truncated operator of [[def-maximal-truncated-singular-integral]].

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Theorem 5.3.4 (Cotlar's inequality) and its proof, printed pp. 364–365

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis
references.locator: Theorem 3.8 (Cotlar's inequality) and its proof, printed pp. 11–12

items.strategy: Decompose the truncated kernel as K_ε=W*φ_ε+(K_ε−W*φ_ε) with a radially decreasing approximate identity φ_ε; the first term is pointwise bounded by ‖φ‖₁M(Tf), while the error kernel has an ε-uniform radially decreasing L¹ majorant ≲(1+|x|)^{−n−δ}, so the domination lemma gives the Mf term with constant C_{n,δ}(A₁+A₂'+A₃).

items.title: Maximal truncations: weak (1,1) and strong Lp bounds
items.statement: Let k and T be as in the Cotlar lemma: pointwise size A₁, standard δ-Hölder smoothness A₂', cancellation A₃, and L² norm B. Then T^* is of weak type (1,1), |{|T^*f|>λ}|≤C_n(A₁+A₂'+A₃+B)λ^{−1}‖f‖₁ for all f∈L¹(ℝ^n) and λ>0, and T^* is bounded on L^p(ℝ^n) for every 1<p<∞ with ‖T^*f‖_p≤C_{n,p}(A₁+A₂'+A₃+B)max(p,(p−1)^{−1})‖f‖_p.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Theorem 5.3.5 and its proof, printed pp. 366–371, and Corollary 5.3.7, printed p. 371

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis
references.locator: Remark 3.9(b) on the weak (1,1) criterion for maximal SIOs, printed p. 12

items.strategy: Cotlar's inequality dominates T^*, hence T^{**}, by M(Tf)+C(A₁+A₂'+A₃)Mf; with T bounded on L^p and M bounded on L^p this yields the strong L^p bounds. For the weak (1,1) bound apply the Calderón–Zygmund decomposition at height γλ, estimate the doubly truncated bad parts using the Hörmander condition supplied by the Hölder kernel, and use the L² bound of T^{**} obtained from Cotlar and the L² bound of M; the pointwise size bound gives T^*≤T^{**}.

items.title: Almost-everywhere convergence of principal-value truncations
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Fix 1≤p<∞, let k and T be as in the maximal-truncation theorem, and let D⊆L^p(ℝ^n) be dense in L^p(ℝ^n) with lim_{ε↓0}T_εf(x) existing for almost every x for every f∈D. Then for every f∈L^p(ℝ^n) the limit lim_{ε↓0}T_εf(x) exists for almost every x. For the Hilbert and Riesz kernels, D=S(ℝ^n) satisfies the hypothesis by the published principal-value kernel formulas.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis
references.locator: Theorem 2.7 (maximal bound plus dense-class convergence) and its proof, printed pp. 4–5

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Corollary 5.3.6 and its proof, printed p. 371, and the cited Theorem 2.1.14

items.strategy: Oscillation argument at the fixed exponent p: for f∈L^p and g∈D the oscillation H(x)=limsup_{ε,θ↓0}|T_εf(x)−T_θf(x)| satisfies H≤2T^*(f−g) pointwise on the set where T_εg converges; for λ>0 the set {H>λ} is contained in {T^*(f−g)>λ/2}, whose measure is controlled by the weak (1,1) bound for p=1 and by Chebyshev together with the strong (p,p) bound for p>1; then let g→f in L^p. No convergence is claimed for a general CZ kernel without the dense-class hypothesis.

items.title: The Hilbert transform is bounded on Lp
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. The Hilbert transform H extends uniquely to a bounded operator on L^p(ℝ) for every 1<p<∞, with norm bounded by a constant depending only on p.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: §5.1.1, kernel and multiplier, printed pp. 314–317; Theorem 5.3.3, printed pp. 359–363

references.title: Richard S. Laugesen, Harmonic Analysis Lecture Notes
references.locator: Chapter 20, Propositions 20.2 and 20.3, printed pp. 113–117

items.strategy: The kernel k(x)=1/(πx) has |k(x)|≤(1/π)|x|^{−1}, and the mean value theorem gives the δ=1 Hölder bound |k(x−y)−k(x)|≤C|y||x|^{−2} for |x|≥2|y|>0, so the Hölder-to-Hörmander lemma supplies the integral condition. The published multiplier and isometry items give the L² bound and the Schwartz-level principal-value formula. The off-support representation for compactly supported f∈L² is proved, not assumed: for φ∈C_c^∞ of the complement of supp f, skew-adjointness and the Schwartz formula identify ⟨Hf,φ⟩ with the absolutely convergent kernel pairing (Fubini over the compact support), so Hf agrees away from supp f with the kernel integral; this is the representation the base Calderón–Zygmund definition requires. Then the strict-range L^p theorem applies.

items.title: The Riesz transforms are bounded on Lp
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let n≥1 and 1≤j≤n. The j-th Riesz transform R_j extends uniquely to a bounded operator on L^p(ℝ^n) for every 1<p<∞, with norm bounded by a constant depending only on n and p.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: §5.1.4, Definition 5.1.13 and Proposition 5.1.14, printed pp. 324–327; Theorem 5.3.3, printed pp. 359–363

references.title: Richard S. Laugesen, Harmonic Analysis Lecture Notes
references.locator: Chapter 20, Proposition 20.3, printed pp. 113–117

items.strategy: The published Riesz kernel estimates give the size bound and the δ=1 first-difference bound for c_nx_j/|x|^{n+1}, and the multiplier definition gives the L² bound; the Hölder-to-Hörmander lemma supplies the integral condition. The Schwartz-level principal-value formula is published. The off-support representation for compactly supported f∈L² is proved from the multiplier definition: R_j*=−R_j because the symbol −iξ_j/|ξ| is purely imaginary, so for test functions supported off supp f the L² pairing is identified with the absolutely convergent kernel integral by Fubini; hence R_j is a Calderón–Zygmund operator and the strict-range L^p theorem applies.

items.title: Dyadic Mihlin pieces: uniform L¹ and first-difference bounds
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\ge1$, put
$n_0:=\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1$, and let $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ be the
smooth step of [[lem-schwartz-cutoffs-from-the-standard-smooth-step]], with
$0\le\chi\le1$, $\chi=1$ on $|\xi|\le1$ and $\chi=0$ on $|\xi|\ge2$. Put
$$\zeta(\xi):=\chi(\xi)-\chi(2\xi).$$
Then $\zeta$ is supported in the annulus $1/2\le|\xi|\le2$, satisfies
$0\le\zeta\le1$, and $\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}\zeta(2^{-j}\xi)=1$ for every
$\xi\ne0$. Let $m$ be a Mihlin symbol with constants $C_\alpha$ as in
[[def-mihlin-symbol-with-more-than-half-dimension-derivatives]], put
$$m_j(\xi):=m(\xi)\,\zeta(2^{-j}\xi),\qquad K_j:=\mathcal F^{-1}\bigl(u_{m_j}\bigr),$$
where $u_{m_j}$ is the regular tempered distribution of $m_j$ and
$\mathcal F^{-1}$ is the inverse Fourier transform of
[[def-fourier-transform-of-a-tempered-distribution]], and let $A$ be any finite
quantity with $A\ge\max\{\|m\|_\infty,\ \max_{|\alpha|\le n_0}C_\alpha\}$. Then
$K_j$ is (the regular distribution of) an $L^2$ function, and there is a
constant $C_n$, depending only on $n$ and on the fixed cutoff $\chi$, such that
$$\sup_{j\in\mathbb Z}\int_{\mathbb R^n}|K_j(x)|\,(1+2^j|x|)^{1/4}\,dx\le C_nA \qquad (1)$$
and
$$\sup_{j\in\mathbb Z}2^{-j}\int_{\mathbb R^n}|\nabla K_j(x)|\,(1+2^j|x|)^{1/4}\,dx\le C_nA. \qquad (2)$$

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.2.7, estimates (6.2.15) and (6.2.16) and derivation (6.2.17)–(6.2.19), printed pp. 446–447

items.strategy: Multiply and divide by (1+2^j|x|)^{n₀}, n₀=⌊n/2⌋+1, apply Cauchy–Schwarz with −2n₀+1/2<−n, expand (1+2^j|x|)^{n₀} in monomials, and use Plancherel plus Leibniz with the Mihlin bounds to obtain O(A2^{jn/2}2^{−j|γ|}) for each γ; the gradient estimate repeats the calculation with ζ_r(ξ)=ξ_rζ(ξ).

items.title: Dyadic Mihlin pieces sum to an off-support kernel representation
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). In the setting of
[[lem-dyadic-mihlin-kernels-have-uniform-integral-hormander-control]] — $m$ a
Mihlin symbol with constants $C_\alpha$
([[def-mihlin-symbol-with-more-than-half-dimension-derivatives]]),
$\zeta$ the annulus cutoff with $\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}\zeta(2^{-j}\xi)=1$ for
$\xi\ne0$, $m_j=m\,\zeta(2^{-j}\cdot)$, $K_j=\mathcal F^{-1}(u_{m_j})$ — the
following hold, with $W:=m^\vee$ and $A\ge\max\{\|m\|_\infty,\max_{|\alpha|\le n_0}C_\alpha\}$:

1. $\sum_{|j|\le N}K_j\to W$ in $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$ as $N\to\infty$;
2. the series $\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}K_j(x)$ converges for almost every
   $x\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$ to a function $k$ that coincides with $W$ on
   $\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$; and
3. that function $k$ satisfies the annular size bound
   $\sup_{\delta>0}\int_{\delta\le|x|\le2\delta}|k(x)|\,dx\le C_nA$ and
   Hörmander's condition
   $\sup_{y\ne0}\int_{|x|\ge2|y|}|k(x-y)-k(x)|\,dx\le C_nA$.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.2.7: the S' convergence, the a.e. convergence of ΣK_j and condition (6.2.20), printed pp. 447–449

items.strategy: Test the partial sums against Schwartz functions to get S' convergence to W; the L¹ bounds with weight (1+2^j|x|)^{±1/4} dominate the tails on |x|≥δ and |x|≤2δ separately, giving absolute convergence of ΣK_j off 0 and the annular size bound; split the Hörmander sum at 2^{−k}≈|y| and use the L¹ bound for j>k and the gradient bound with the mean value theorem for j≤k.

items.title: The Mihlin–Hörmander Fourier multiplier theorem
items.statement: Let m be bounded on ℝ^n and satisfy |∂^αm(ξ)|≤C_α|ξ|^{−|α|} for every |α|≤⌊n/2⌋+1 and ξ≠0. Then m is an L^p Fourier multiplier for every 1<p<∞, and there is a constant C_n with ‖T_mf‖_p≤C_nmax(p,(p−1)^{−1})(A+‖m‖_∞)‖f‖_p for all f∈L^p(ℝ^n), where A is the Mihlin constant assembled from the C_α.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Theorem 6.2.7 and its proof, printed pp. 445–450

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis
references.locator: Theorem 3.13 (Mihlin multiplier theorem), printed p. 13

items.strategy: Boundedness of m gives the L² bound for T_m; the dyadic pieces produce a kernel k coinciding with m^∨ off 0 with annular size and Hörmander bounds, hence a Calderón–Zygmund kernel with T_m as its operator; apply the strict-range L^p theorem. No endpoint claim.

items.title: Endpoint targets: weak (1,1) here, L∞ to BMO later, never strong (1,1) or L∞
items.statement: For an L²-bounded Calderón–Zygmund operator the two endpoint targets are the weak (1,1) estimate proved on this page and the L∞→BMO estimate that is the subject of the later BMO page of this track; neither a strong L¹ bound nor an L∞ bound is claimed here.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: §5.3, weak (1,1) in Theorem 5.3.3 and the strict-range scope of (5.3.14), printed pp. 355–371

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4
references.locator: §3 on BMO as the endpoint substitute, printed p. 10

items.strategy: Roadmap only: point at the proved weak (1,1) estimate and at the later BMO page; state explicitly that no strong L¹ or L∞ conclusion is part of this page. No new mathematical assertion is made, so no proof section is required.

items.title: Mihlin endpoints: weak (1,1), but no general strong endpoint bounds
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). The displayed estimate in
[[thm-mihlin-fourier-multiplier-theorem]] gives strong $L^p$ bounds for
$1<p<\infty$. Its proof also identifies $T_m$ as a Calderón–Zygmund operator
with Hörmander constant at most $C_nA$ and $L^2$ norm $\|m\|_\infty$.
Consequently [[thm-calderon-zygmund-operator-has-weak-type-one-one]] gives the
weak endpoint
$$|\{|T_mf|>\lambda\}|\le C_n(A+\|m\|_\infty)\lambda^{-1}\|f\|_1\qquad(f\in L^1,\ \lambda>0),$$
where $A$ is the derivative-bound constant in the Mihlin theorem. This is a
bound for the multiplier operator; it does not require the stronger
principal-value and pointwise kernel hypotheses used for maximal truncations.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Theorem 6.2.7, printed p. 446, including its weak (1,1) conclusion; Theorem 5.3.3, printed pp. 359–362

items.strategy: Scope remark: derive weak (1,1) from the proved Mihlin Calderón–Zygmund operator representation; distinguish general strong endpoint failures using orientation-only later Hilbert examples.

title: Calderon Zygmund Decomposition and Singular Integrals — Examples

items.title: Calderón–Zygmund decomposition of an interval indicator
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Take f=1_{(0,1]} on ℝ with the half-open all-generation dyadic grid (a,b] of [[def-dyadic-cube-in-rn-all-generations]] and λ=1/4. The unique maximal dyadic interval with average of |f| above λ is (0,2], whose average is 1/2=2λ; the bad part is b=(1/2)1_{(0,1]}−(1/2)1_{(1,2]} and the good part is g=(1/2)1_{(0,2]}, so |g|=2λ, ∫b=0 and Σ|Q|=2≤λ^{−1}‖f‖₁=4. The parent (0,4] of the maximal bad interval has average exactly λ and is therefore good, which is how the 2λ average bound is attained.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: Theorem 5.3.1 scope, printed pp. 355–357; the computation is direct

items.strategy: Work in the half-open grid: a dyadic interval is (m2^{−k},(m+1)2^{−k}], so intervals of all generations occur. The interval (0,1] has average 1 and its parent (0,2] has average 1/2>λ, while the next ancestor (0,4] has average exactly λ and is good; every other dyadic interval meeting (0,2] has average 0 or fails to contain a subset of (0,2] of full measure, so (0,2] is the unique maximal bad interval. Read off b and g from the formulas in the decomposition lemma and check |g|=1/2=2λ, ∫b=0 and Σ|Q|=2≤λ^{−1}‖f‖₁=4. This is a finite verification of maximality, the 2^nλ bound and the parent-good property.

items.title: The Riesz kernel is a standard Calderón–Zygmund kernel
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For n≥1 and 1≤j≤n the Riesz kernel K_j(x)=c_nx_j/|x|^{n+1} satisfies the pointwise size bound |K_j(x)|≤c_n|x|^{−n}, the δ=1 first-difference bound on |x|≥2|y|>0, and the zero spherical-mean estimate; the Riesz transform R_j is L²-bounded and the published principal-value formula identifies its truncations on Schwartz functions. Hence R_j is a standard-kernel Calderón–Zygmund operator in the sense of this page, and the strict-range L^p theorem applies to it.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: §5.1.4, Definition 5.1.13, Proposition 5.1.14 and the estimates in its proof, printed pp. 324–327

references.title: Richard S. Laugesen, Harmonic Analysis Lecture Notes
references.locator: Chapter 20, Proposition 20.3, printed pp. 113–117

items.strategy: Use the published raw size, difference and spherical-mean estimates. Integrate the raw difference bound by polar coordinates to establish the Hormander condition before asserting standard-kernel status. The L2 multiplier is skew-adjoint; its Schwartz principal-value formula and the real odd kernel yield the off-essential-support representation by Fubini and distribution injectivity.

items.title: Strong type (1,1) fails for the Hilbert transform
items.statement: The interval indicator f=1_{(0,1]} lies in L¹(ℝ), but its Hilbert transform is Hf(x)=π^{−1}log|x/(x−1)| for x∉{0,1}, which is not integrable because |Hf(x)|≳1/|x| for large x. Hence the Hilbert transform has no compatible strong type (1,1) extension: there is no bounded L¹→L¹ extension agreeing with the L² Hilbert transform on L¹∩L². No weak (1,1) estimate is refuted here; the Hilbert transform is a Calderón–Zygmund operator and this page proves the weak endpoint instead.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: §5.1.1, Example 5.1.3 scope, printed pp. 314–317

references.title: Richard S. Laugesen, Harmonic Analysis Lecture Notes
references.locator: Chapter 20, computation of the interval transform, printed pp. 113–119

items.strategy: Use the published computation q=Hf=π^{−1}log|x/(x−1)| of the interval indicator. Since q(x)∼±1/(πx) as |x|→∞, q is not in L¹: ∫_{|x|≥R}|q|≳∫_{|x|≥R}dx/|x|=∞. A bounded L¹ extension T agreeing with the L² transform on L¹∩L² would make Tf an L¹ class equal a.e. to q, contradicting the failure of integrability. The contrast with the weak (1,1) bound is a pointer only and is not used in the refutation.

items.title: Calderón–Zygmund operators need not map L∞ to L∞
items.statement: The bounded function f=1_{(0,1]} has compatible Hilbert transform q(x)=π^{−1}log|x/(x−1)|, which is essentially unbounded near 0 and near 1: q(x)→−∞ as x→0 and q(x)→+∞ as x→1. Therefore no bounded L∞→L∞ extension agrees with the L² Hilbert transform on L∞∩L², and L∞ need not be mapped to L∞ by a Calderón–Zygmund operator. No BMO-valued endpoint estimate is refuted or asserted here.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: §5.1.1 and Remark 5.1.9 on endpoint behaviour, printed pp. 314–322

references.title: Richard S. Laugesen, Harmonic Analysis Lecture Notes
references.locator: Chapter 20, interval transform, printed pp. 113–119

items.strategy: Read the logarithmic divergence off the same interval transform: as x→0⁺ the value π^{−1}log(x/(1−x))→−∞ and as x→1 the value diverges to +∞, so the a.e. defined transform is not essentially bounded; a bounded L∞ extension is impossible.

items.title: Size without cancellation does not give a principal value
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. The positive kernel k(x)=|x|^{−n} satisfies the pointwise size bound |k(x)|=|x|^{−n}, but its symmetric truncations diverge: for f=1_{B(0,1)} one has T_εf(0)=∫_{ε<|y|<1}|y|^{−n}dy=|S^{n−1}|log(1/ε)→∞ as ε↓0. Hence the pointwise size condition alone gives neither a principal-value distribution along this sequence nor a finite maximal truncated operator, and the Hörmander/cancellation hypothesis is not redundant.

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: §5.3.2, conditions (5.3.4)–(5.3.12) and the role of cancellation, printed pp. 358–359

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4
references.locator: Remark 2.5 on the logarithmic Schur-test divergence and the need for cancellation, printed p. 6

items.strategy: Evaluate the annular integral in polar coordinates: ∫_{ε<|y|<1}|y|^{−n}dy=|S^{n−1}|∫_ε^1r^{−1}dr=|S^{n−1}|log(1/ε), which diverges as ε↓0; compare with the convergence of the truncated kernel in L^{p'} used to define T_ε for kernels with size alone when the singular part is cut off, and record that the untruncated principal value fails.

items.title: Newtonian Hessian kernels fit the Calderón–Zygmund framework
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let n≥3 and let Γ be the Newtonian potential normalised by −ΔΓ=δ₀. The distributional Hessian satisfies ∂_{ij}Γ=p.v.∂_{ij}Γ−(δ_{ij}/n)δ₀, where the singular part is the principal value of the function k_{ij}(x)=∂_{ij}Γ(x)=σ_{n−1}^{−1}(nx_ix_j|x|^{−n−2}−δ_{ij}|x|^{−n}) on ℝ^n\{0}, which is smooth and homogeneous of degree −n with |k_{ij}(x)|≤(1+n)σ_{n−1}^{−1}|x|^{−n}, first differences ≲|y||x|^{−n−1} on |x|≥2|y|>0, and zero spherical mean. Hence the singular part of the second derivatives of the Newtonian potential is a standard Calderón–Zygmund kernel after the local delta term is removed, and its principal-value operator is L²-bounded with symbol −ξ_iξ_j/|ξ|²+δ_{ij}/n.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations, revised 18 June 2014
references.locator: §2.7.1, Theorem 2.26 and its proof (second derivatives of the Newtonian potential), printed pp. 37–38

references.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition
references.locator: §5.2, homogeneous kernels with zero spherical mean, printed pp. 333–353

items.strategy: With Γ(x)=((n−2)σ_{n−1})^{−1}|x|^{2−n} (so that −ΔΓ=δ₀ by the published Newtonian-potential items), differentiate twice to get k_{ij}; check the size bound and the gradient bound (which gives the first-difference bound by the mean value theorem on |x|≥2|y|), and verify ∫_{S^{n−1}}(nω_iω_j−δ_{ij})dσ=0 via ∫ω_iω_jdσ=σ_{n−1}δ_{ij}/n. The local term is identified by summing the diagonal relation, which gives ΔΓ=−δ₀ and hence the coefficient −1/n; the p.v. operator is L²-bounded because its symbol is −ξ_iξ_j/|ξ|²+δ_{ij}/n, the symbol of R_iR_j+(δ_{ij}/n)I.
